decision: Split rlsentry into a chain; first task is anon-probe (live black-box scan with anon key)
why: The request is a whole product; the black-box probe is what directly answers "verification, not reminders" and fixes the verdict/report model the rest builds on

decision: Write probe on by default but must never persist a row; uncertain → verdict unknown
why: Write exposure is half the CVE; scanning real prod data makes persistence the worst-case failure

decision: Reports never contain row values, only table, columns, row count
why: Exposed rows are likely third-party PII and reports land in CI logs

decision: No service-role key accepted in this task
why: Scan must see exactly what an outsider sees; avoids handling a secret
